paragraphs.heading: Rock worth digging up
paragraphs.text: Ore is natural rock or sediment holding one or more valuable minerals, which typically include metals. Two things make it ore: the minerals are concentrated above background levels, and the rock is economically viable to mine and process. The word is of Anglo-Saxon origin and means "lump of metal".

paragraphs.heading: Grade and the cost test
paragraphs.text: Ore grade is the concentration of the desired material in the rock. To decide whether a rock is of high enough grade to be worth mining, the value of its metals or minerals has to be weighed against what extraction would cost. Rock that passes this test is considered an ore. An ore deposit is an accumulation of minerals inside a host rock that is economically significant.

paragraphs.heading: Ore minerals and gangue
paragraphs.text: The minerals of interest are, as a rule, oxides, sulfides and silicates, along with native metals like copper or gold. A complex ore is one that holds more than one valuable mineral. In most cases an ore is not made entirely of a single mineral. Other valuable minerals are mixed in, together with rocks and minerals that are unwanted or have no value. The portion of an ore that has no economic appeal, and that mining cannot avoid, is called gangue.

paragraphs.heading: From mine to metal
paragraphs.text: Ore is taken from the earth by mining, then treated or refined, often by smelting, to extract the valuable metals or minerals. Separating the ore minerals from the gangue minerals is known as mineral processing or ore dressing. It consists of liberation, which frees the ore from the gangue, and then concentration, which separates out the desired mineral or minerals. The operations used include froth flotation, gravity concentration, and electric or magnetic methods. Once processed, the gangue is known as tailings, a useless but potentially harmful material made in great quantity, above all from lower grade deposits.

paragraphs.heading: Ores from igneous rock
paragraphs.text: Ore bodies form through various geological processes, which together are generally called ore genesis. Pegmatites are igneous rocks with very coarse grains. They crystallize slowly at great depth, which leads to their very large crystals, and they are a big source of industrial minerals, with quartz, feldspar and spodumene among them. Carbonatites are igneous rocks in which carbonate minerals make up over 50% of the volume. No other igneous rock contains as many rare earth elements, and carbonatites are a major source of the light rare earth elements.

paragraphs.heading: Chromium and diamonds
paragraphs.text: Chromite is the only ore of chromium. Stratiform chromites are one source of it. Their name comes from their strata-like shape and from the way they form, by layered magmatic injection into the host rock. The most famous example is the Bushveld Complex in South Africa. Kimberlites are a primary source for diamonds, and their origin lies at depths of 150 km in the mantle.
